Judge: A is better in all four pairs, and none is close. The B frames share one set of problems. The characters look like avatars: smooth plastic faces, smeared or simplified cloth, and stiff walks with hands locked at the hips, little stride and no arm swing. Sterile, mechanically repeating paving fills the lower third of most shots. Some assets are unfinished: flat-colour untextured boxes, an untextured awning plane, a stray geometry sliver and a faceted, blotchy-shaded car with a blank plate. The few NPCs are near-clones, the streets have little life, and the lighting is pleasant but generic, with no narrative hook in any frame. B does show a credible sense of place (shophouse facades, legible shop signs, landmark skylines, warm late light with long shadows), but no B frame wows. The A frames win on heavy weathering and grime, dense layered set dressing, coherent material response (car paint, chrome, brick, cloth), character fidelity and expression, and deliberate cinematic composition (low hero angles, a dutch tilt, story moments such as the burning SUV). Pair 1 A is the weakest A frame: dated textures, and its strength is density rather than polish. Priorities for B, in order: remove every placeholder and untextured asset, and fix vehicle normals and reflections; raise character fidelity and give the walk real stride and arm swing; break up the ground plane with wear, decals and kerb detail; fill the mid-ground with varied NPCs, vehicles and street furniture; then compose shots around a focal subject with key or rim light.
